name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent David Taylor running with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger has raised only about $1,000
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
model.rationale: The district's R+21 lean, an incumbent Republican with over $1 million raised against a challenger who has raised barely $1,000, and markets pricing a Republican win at 98% all point the same way. No evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any sign of Democratic fundraising or outside spending entering the district would be the first hint of competitiveness, but none exists now.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwestern Ohio's 2nd District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent David Taylor is seeking re-election after winning the seat in 2024, and he holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised about $1.1 million with $443,000 on hand.

His Democratic opponent, Jennifer Mazzuckelli, has raised just over $1,000 and reported only $219 in cash, indicating a minimal campaign operation. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 98% chance of holding the seat. Absent unexpected developments, Taylor is heavily favored to win re-election.
